observations:
Torah #157 is a 2-sentence teaching yielding exactly one conceptual cluster. All bechina-language identifications in the source text belong to a single unified domain: the state of Torah-attachment (דְּבֵקוּת לְדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה מִפִּי הַצַּדִּיק) as world-transcendence (נוֹטֵל חַיָּיו מִן הָעוֹלָם). This domain is fully represented by Package 1 in torah_157_packages.json.

The requirement for a new package is: 3+ bechina-connected concepts forming an independent domain not captured by existing packages. Torah #157 contains only 3 nodes total in its bechina layer — all within Package 1. No subset of those nodes forms an independent domain.

Three candidate areas were examined and ruled out:

(1) A 'Tzaddik as teacher' package: The Tzaddik (הַצַּדִּיק) is named as the channel of Torah words. One might propose a separate package around the Tzaddik's role. However: (a) the Tzaddik is not given a bechina-identity declaration in this Torah — he is mentioned relationally, not equated with another concept via bechina language; (b) no second bechina-connected concept around the Tzaddik exists in the text (the Teaching says 'through the Tzaddik's mouth' — one functional mention, not a bechina cluster); (c) fewer than 3 nodes are available, so no independent package can be constituted. The Tzaddik's role here is the channel through which Torah-attachment occurs — this is an eitza-adjacent structure (Torah words flow from the Tzaddik's mouth as the cause of the student's attachment), not a bechina-identity cluster. Ruled out.

(2) A 'worldly life / material existence' evil-mirror package: The teaching implicitly contrasts Torah-attachment (the elevated state) with continued desire for worldly life (the unelevated state). One might propose an evil-mirror package centered on חַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה (life of this world) and related concepts. However: (a) the Rebbe does not give worldly life any bechina-identity declaration — he simply states that the Torah-attached person cannot tolerate it; (b) no second node is bechina-identified with worldly life; (c) the negative pole in this teaching is entirely implicit and rhetorical — the Rebbe's amazement ('תָּמֵהַּ אֲנִי') at how worldly life could still be desired is not a bechina declaration about the nature of worldly life but an expression of astonishment at its persistence despite Torah-attachment. No evil-domain bechina cluster can be constituted. Ruled out.

(3) A 'hermeneutical re-reading' or 'Mishnah-as-bechina' meta-package: One might propose that the Rebbe's practice of re-reading Mishnaic/Talmudic texts as bechina-expressions of spiritual states constitutes a separate conceptual domain. But this is a methodological observation about the Rebbe's teaching style, not a new conceptual package within Torah #157. The 'וְזֶהוּ' formula is a linking mechanism, not a new domain. Ruled out.

Conclusion: Torah #157 contains exactly one bechina-connected cluster (Package 1: Torah-attachment as world-transcendence). Its extreme brevity — 2 sentences — makes it structurally the simplest Torah in the corpus from a package-analysis perspective. One package, one domain, no subdivisions, no evil mirror with bechina language. The teaching's power lies not in structural complexity but in the depth of a single aphoristic identity claim, signaled by the closing 'וְהָבֵן הֵיטֵב' (understand this well).
